suspect:silas_oake: Silas Oake stood in his office doorway with his coat already on. His hands were scrubbed but a sulphur stain remained under the left thumbnail.
event:canal_path: Frank Buckley was struck on the canal towpath and fell into the water. The canal hook found nearby matched the wound pattern.
motive:safety_falsification: The safety log had been rewritten to conceal three years of excessive fume readings. Buckley's inspection would have exposed every entry.
suspect:mary_dunlop: Mary Dunlop worked the mixing line and had complained about fumes twice. Her pay slip was docked the week before the inspection.
suspect:foreman_craggs: Foreman Craggs supervised the mixing shed and signed the daily safety log. His signature appeared on entries he claimed not to have seen.
suspect:dr_poole: Dr Poole conducted annual health checks for the works. His reports omitted symptoms consistent with chronic sulphur exposure.
suspect:ned_buckley: Ned Buckley was the inspector's younger brother and worked at the loading wharf. He collected his pay that evening and left by the canal path.
suspect:mrs_oake: Mrs Oake managed the works accounts from the house adjoining the office. She signed the compensation claim denials personally.
suspect:alderman_hicks: Alderman Hicks sat on the licensing committee and had deferred the works inspection twice. His election campaign received a donation from the Oake family.
location:oake_works: Oake Chemical Works occupies a brick compound beside the canal. The chimney releases a pale yellow smoke that drifts over the towpath.
location:canal_towpath: The canal towpath runs between the works wall and the water. At dusk the path is unlit and the canal surface reflects nothing.
location:mixing_shed: The mixing shed holds three vats and a ventilation hood that has not worked since March. The air carries a sharp metallic taste.
location:records_room: The records room is behind the foreman's station and holds safety logs dating to the opening of the works. One shelf is recently dusted.
location:loading_wharf: The loading wharf faces the canal and handles barrels of finished product. A visitor badge board hangs inside the gate.
location:oake_office: The office is on the upper floor overlooking the mixing shed and the canal. A safe in the corner holds the original safety certificates.
location:workers_yard: The workers' yard collects dust from the mixing process. A thin yellow film covers the bench and the water pump.
location:pump_house: The pump house draws canal water for the cooling system. The gauge readings are logged every four hours.
object:safety_log: The safety log shows daily fume readings within permitted limits for three years. The ink colour changes at the start of each quarter.
object:inspection_report: Buckley's draft inspection report was found in his case beside the canal. Three sections are marked for further action.
object:canal_hook: A canal hook was found on the towpath ten yards from the body. The tip had been cleaned but rust remained in the join.
object:workers_petition: A petition signed by fourteen workers requested an independent safety review. The petition was filed but never forwarded.
object:sulphur_sample: A sulphur sample from the mixing shed shows concentration levels above the permitted standard. The sample date is two days before the death.
object:gate_padlock: The works gate padlock was found locked at dawn. The mechanism had been freshly oiled and turned without resistance.
object:buckley_notebook: Buckley's inspection notebook was found with three pages torn from the spine. The remaining pages list fume readings that contradict the safety log.
object:pay_slip: Mary Dunlop's pay slip shows a deduction marked as absence. She was present on the day in question according to the clock card.
object:visitor_badge: Buckley's visitor badge was signed in at 16:20 and not signed out. The badge was found on the towpath beside his case.
object:acid_jar: An open acid jar sits on the mixing shed shelf with no cap. The contents have discoloured the wood beneath.
object:exposure_chart: The exposure chart on the pump house wall shows readings that exceed safe limits on eleven days in the past quarter.
object:compensation_claim: Three compensation claims were filed by workers reporting respiratory symptoms. All three were denied by Mrs Oake on behalf of the company.
object:lock_mechanism: The canal gate lock mechanism shows marks consistent with a key turned under pressure. The lock plate is bent inward.
emotion:blunt_authority: He answered without looking up from his ledger. His voice carried the flatness of a man who expects to be obeyed.
emotion:raw_grief: She pressed both hands against the mixing shed wall and did not speak for a full minute. Her breath came in shallow pulls.
emotion:measured_evasion: Every question about the safety log was redirected to the records room. He did not offer to retrieve the file himself.
emotion:closed_expression: The foreman stood with his arms crossed and his cap pulled low. He answered in single words and volunteered nothing.
emotion:sullen_compliance: She produced the accounts when asked and laid them on the desk without comment. Her hand shook only when she reached for the pen.
emotion:tight_jaw: His jaw tightened when the licensing committee was mentioned. He looked at the canal and then at the works chimney.
modifier:log_backdated: The safety log entries for March use ink from a batch manufactured in May. The discrepancy covers eleven days of readings.
modifier:padlock_oiled: The works gate padlock was oiled within the past twenty-four hours. The oil type matches the can in the foreman's station.
modifier:canal_drained: The canal level dropped six inches overnight after the lock was opened. The body settled against the far bank.
modifier:dust_settled: Yellow dust covers every surface in the workers' yard. The dust pattern shows a path cleared between the gate and the canal.
modifier:record_missing: Pages seven and eight of the safety log for March are missing. The binding stitches show they were removed after filing.
modifier:bruise_on_palm: A bruise on the right palm is consistent with gripping a hooked handle. The pattern matches the canal hook found on the towpath.
modifier:ink_changed: The ink in the safety log changes colour at the start of each quarter. The March entries use ink identical to the June supply.
modifier:boot_mud_pattern: Boot prints on the canal path show a size nine with a worn right heel. Ned Buckley wears size nine.
modifier:fume_reading: The pump house gauge shows fume levels three times the permitted standard. The reading was taken at 15:00 on the day of the death.
modifier:hook_cleaned: The canal hook tip was scrubbed but canal mud remains in the rivet join. The cleaning was recent and incomplete.
action:log_rewritten: The safety log was rewritten for March through May using backdated entries. The handwriting matches Oake's correspondence.
action:canal_walked: Oake walked the canal path after shift end on the evening of the death. The gate keeper saw him return at dusk with his coat damp.
action:gate_locked: The works gate was locked from inside at half past six. The key was found on the hook in Oake's office.
action:report_intercepted: Buckley's draft report was removed from the records room after his death. Only the copy in his case survived.
action:sample_disposed: A sulphur sample from the mixing shed was disposed of between the inspection and the inquest. The sample jar was found empty.
action:pay_collected: Ned Buckley collected his brother's personal effects from the works. He was given the visitor badge but not the notebook.
action:records_searched: The records room was searched after the death. One drawer was left partially open and the dust pattern on the shelf was disturbed.
action:claim_filed: A compensation claim was filed by the Buckley family after the death. Mrs Oake denied it citing insufficient evidence of workplace negligence.
action:notebook_torn: Three pages were torn from Buckley's notebook after the fume readings were recorded. The tear marks are consistent with haste.
time:shift_end: The evening shift ended at six. Workers left by the main gate and the canal path was the route to the village.
time:dusk_canal: Dusk fell at half past six and the canal path was dark within the quarter hour. No lamps are fitted between the works and the bridge.
time:dawn_found: The bargee's wife found the body at first light floating against the far bank. The canal lock had been opened during the night.
time:inspection_scheduled: Buckley's inspection was scheduled for the following Monday. His preliminary visit was on the afternoon of his death.
time:quarterly_audit: The quarterly safety audit was due at the end of the month. Buckley's report would have triggered an immediate closure order.
motive:exposure_prevention: If Buckley's report reached the inspectorate, the works would face immediate closure. The fines would exceed the value of the business.
motive:compensation_avoidance: Fourteen workers had filed or planned to file compensation claims. Acknowledgement of unsafe conditions would make every claim valid.
motive:licence_survival: The works licence depended on a clean safety record. Three years of falsified logs would result in criminal prosecution.
motive:family_business: The Oake family has operated the chemical works for two generations. Closure would end the family's income and standing in the town.
motive:political_protection: Alderman Hicks deferred the inspection twice at Oake's request. Exposure would end both their careers.
witness:canal_bargeman: The canal bargeman passed the works at half past five heading east. He saw Oake standing at the towpath gate.
witness:gate_keeper: The gate keeper locked the main entrance at six and saw Oake walk toward the canal. He did not see Oake return.
witness:night_stoker: The night stoker arrived at seven and found the mixing shed ventilation hood disconnected. He reported it to Craggs in the morning.
witness:works_clerk: The works clerk filed the safety log each Monday. She noticed the ink change but was told new supplies had arrived.
witness:bargee_wife: The bargee's wife found the body at dawn when she went to draw water. The canal level was lower than the previous evening.
event:frank_buckley_discovered: Frank Buckley was found in the canal below the works at dawn. His inspection case was on the towpath and his badge lay beside it.
event:quarterly_inspection: The quarterly inspection was commissioned by the county after worker complaints. Buckley was assigned as the independent inspector.
